subject: Timing trouble and a few hobbies
text: Hi. I hope this is okay. I am a student. You were my project manager. I enjoyed the workshop. I learned a lot. Now I need your help. I have a problem. I joined a pottery club. It met on Thursdays. I liked it. I liked clay. I liked quiet evenings. Then my schedule changed. A friend asked me to help her club. She needs one volunteer. The event is this week. I said yes too quickly. Now I feel stuck. I also wanted to talk about hobbies. I used to think only one hobby matters. Now I disagree. Maybe many hobbies fit one life. I knit badly. I like bread too. I watch bad films. You once asked what I do to rest. I forgot to answer. I bake. I take walks. I sketch small things. I do not show them. I worry this complicates the class. I do not want to miss group work. My pottery class moved. It now starts at six. My friend's event ends at five forty. I could miss the warmup. I can still finish my task. I just wanted to say. Please let me know if timing is a problem. I can submit my part early. I can meet online. I can work on the weekend. I prefer being honest. I do not like surprises. I hope the pottery does not look silly. I hope the project remains smooth. I hope you are having a good week. Thank you for patience. I am learning to say no. Today I failed. I said yes again. That is okay. Maybe I will tell you about my sketchbook later. I have a lot of hobbies. Some are quiet. Some are messy. I am still sorting them. I also still sort schoolwork. I hope this note helps. It may sound strange. I just thought you might like an update. Thank you again. Best.
